text:
Marathon Petroleum fell slightly today as crude oil prices dropped on Monday following reports of potential U.S.-Iran diplomatic talks. Oil fell to session lows amid hopes for peaceful resolution in the Middle East, which reduces the geopolitical premium that has been supporting energy prices. A refiner's profitability depends partly on the spread between crude costs and what it can sell refined products for, so lower oil prices can compress those margins even if refined product prices don't fall as much.

The stock is also down 6.5% over two weeks following a leadership change announced on October 29th and amid broader caution from analysts about Big Oil earnings guidance. While refineries are running at a healthy 92.8% utilization, the uncertainty around management transitions and forward guidance—combined with the sudden shift in oil market sentiment from geopolitical risk to diplomacy hopes—has weighed on the share price.
